title: Intake orchestration and enterprise-priority matrix for hosted chat/streaming/tool-calls
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Create a repeatable intake orchestration and scoring matrix for feature requests that touch hosted chat, streaming, function/tool calling, and structured outputs. Goal is to reduce ambiguity in triage decisions for enterprise customers (SAML, compliance, SLAs, private deployments) and provide a single source-of-truth workflow that PMs, Solutions Engineering, and Sales can use during intake calls.

Background: We are seeing an increase in feature asks from enterprise accounts that combine several concerns: streaming (low-latency expectations), tool/function calling (security & auditing), and structured outputs (schema guarantees and validation). Current intake is ad-hoc: tickets land across multiple channels (Zendesk, email, sales notes, account execs) and are triaged inconsistently. This work builds an orchestration layer (process + rubric + tooling checklist) to standardize scoring and routing of requests.

Scope: This ticket covers the triage matrix, intake form fields, escalation routes, SLAs for initial response, and a lightweight automation spec (workflows for Jira/Linear labels and Slack routing). Implementation of backend automation (Connectors, webhooks) is tracked separately.
acceptance_criteria: A documented prioritization rubric with weighted scoring fields for enterprise-specific signals (security/compliance, SLA risk, revenue, engineering effort, user impact)
An intake form template (Confluence + Google Form) and Linear labels mapping that PMs and SEs can use in discovery calls
A documented routing table: automatic fast-track, sales escalation, design review, security review, or product backlog with clear owners and SLAs
prioritization_rubric: Score components (example): Revenue potential (0-10) * 0.25 + Customer Criticality (0-10) * 0.25 + Compliance/Security Risk (0-10) * 0.20 + Engineering Effort (0-10, inverted) * 0.15 + Strategic Alignment (0-10) * 0.15. Special rule: any item with Compliance/Security Risk >= 8 triggers mandatory security review and cannot be auto-accepted. Fast-track if score >= 8.5 and revenue potential >=7 and customer is Enterprise+ with contract renewal within 6 months.
proposed_workflow_steps: 1) Intake received via canonical form or forwarded from Sales/SE. Required fields: customer tier, SLA expectations, data residency, required approvals, ROI/renewal windows, sample prompt or use-case, desired latency and concurrency.
2) Auto-populate Linear ticket with labels and initial score using the rubric; send notification to #pm-intake Slack channel.
3) PM reviews within 48h and assigns: Fast-track (assign PM+EM), Security review, Design research, or Backlog.
4) If Security review required, Security team has 5 business days to respond with risk level and remediation estimate.
5) For Fast-track items, create a scoped PRD stub, schedule a 30-minute cross-functional sync, and add to the next sprint planning buffer or create a dedicated runway for Dedicated/Private work.
6) Track outcome metrics monthly: intake volume, time-to-first-response, percent fast-tracked, and downstream engineering slippage.
7) Close-loop: Customer-facing owner (AE/CS) must be notified within SLA and given expected delivery window or compensating workaround.
8) Add an index entry in Confluence for all triaged enterprise requests for quarterly prioritization reviews.
Note: automation tasks (webhooks, label mapping) are tracked in ENG-39722 and will be integrated after rubric sign-off.
